title: Parameterized ALU
constraints: Parameter `WIDTH` (default 8) sets the width of `a`, `b` and `y`. The judge instantiates the ALU with **WIDTH = 16**.
Shift amounts use the low log₂(WIDTH) bits of `b`. Opcodes 11–15 produce `y = 0`.
`carry`: the carry-out for ADD. For SUB it is the carry-out of `a + ~b + 1`, i.e. 1 when `a ≥ b` unsigned. It is 0 for all other ops.
`overflow`: signed overflow for ADD and SUB, 0 otherwise. `zero = (y == 0)`, `negative = y[WIDTH-1]` for every op.
hints: Compute the add/subtract once, in WIDTH+1 bits, with `b` inverted and a carry-in of 1 for SUB. Bit WIDTH is then the carry.
Signed overflow: the operands (after inverting `b` for SUB) have equal signs, and the result's sign differs.
SRA needs a signed shift: `$signed(a) >>> shamt` in Verilog, `shift_right(signed(a), n)` in VHDL. Use `$clog2(WIDTH)` for the shift-amount width.
